(sec-item-nodeuser)=
# NodeUser

A node with any number of {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` coordinates, whose position, and optionally orientation, are computed from its coordinates by Python user functions: a node for elements whose nodes are not in Exudyn, such as an ANCF node with full gradients. The node markers (MarkerNodePosition, MarkerNodeRigid, MarkerNodeCoordinate), SensorNode, loads on these markers and every connector work on it.

## Interface

- Provides: `Position`, `Orientation`
- Node markers that can be attached: [](#sec-item-markernodeposition), [](#sec-item-markernoderigid), [](#sec-item-markernoderotationcoordinate)
- Objects that take this node: [](#sec-item-objectmasspoint), [](#sec-item-objectbeamgeometricallyexact)

## Parameters

The parameters of the item; in a dictionary, its type is 'User':

| name | type | size | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **name** | String |  | '' | node's unique name |
| **numberOfODE2Coordinates** | PInt |  | 0 | (symbol: $n$) number of {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` coordinates; **must be given**: the default is only a placeholder |
| **referenceCoordinates** | Vector |  | [] | (symbol: $\qv\cRef \in \Rcal^n$) reference coordinates of the node; must have numberOfODE2Coordinates components |
| **initialCoordinates** | Vector |  | [] | (symbol: $\qv\cIni \in \Rcal^n$) initial displacement coordinates; must have numberOfODE2Coordinates components |
| **initialVelocities** | Vector |  | [] | (symbol: $\dot\qv\cIni \in \Rcal^n$) initial velocity coordinates; must have numberOfODE2Coordinates components |
| **parameters** | NumpyVector |  | [] | (symbol: $\pv_{par} \in \Rcal^{n_p}$) the parameters of the node, passed to every user function; their meaning is defined by the user functions, see exudyn.advancedUtilities.ParameterLayout; empty by default |
| **positionUserFunction** | NodeUserPositionUserFunction |  | 0 | (symbol: $\LU{0}{\pv}(\qv)$) A Python user function which computes the global position of the node; it must be given |
| **positionJacobianUserFunction** | NodeUserPositionJacobianUserFunction |  | 0 | (symbol: $\Jm_{pos}(\qv) \in \Rcal^{3\times n}$) A Python user function which computes the position Jacobian; by central differences of the position if not given |
| **rotationMatrixUserFunction** | NodeUserRotationMatrixUserFunction |  | 0 | (symbol: $\LU{0n}{\Rot}(\qv) \in \Rcal^{3\times 3}$) A Python user function which computes the rotation matrix of the node; optional, for rigid markers |
| **rotationJacobianUserFunction** | NodeUserRotationJacobianUserFunction |  | 0 | (symbol: $\Jm_{rot}(\qv) \in \Rcal^{3\times n}$) A Python user function which computes the rotation Jacobian (of the global angular velocity); by central differences of the rotation matrix if not given |
| **visualization** | VNodeUser |  |  | parameters for visualization of item |

## Visualization parameters

The parameters of `VNodeUser`, given as `visualization`:

| name | type | size | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **show** | Bool |  | True | set true, if item is shown in visualization and false if it is not shown |
| **drawSize** | float |  | -1. | drawing size (diameter, dimensions of underlying cube, etc.) for item; size == -1.f means that default size is used |
| **color** | Float4 | 4 | [-1.,-1.,-1.,-1.] | Default RGBA color for nodes; 4th value is alpha-transparency; R=-1.f means, that default color is used |

## Drawing

Drawn as [all nodes](#sec-drawing-nodes); a point at its position; with `nodes.showBasis` and a `rotationMatrixUserFunction`, also its frame.

Settings beyond those of all nodes: [`general.axesTiling`](#sec-vsettingsgeneral), [`nodes.basisSize`](#sec-vsettingsnodes), [`nodes.showBasis`](#sec-vsettingsnodes).

## Output variables

Available as `OutputVariableType` in sensors, `Get...Output()` and other functions:

```{tabularcolumns} \Y{0.25}\Y{0.25}\Y{0.5}
```

| output variable | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| Position | $\LU{0}{\pv}\cConfig$ | global position of the node, from positionUserFunction |
| Displacement | $\LU{0}{\pv}\cConfig - \LU{0}{\pv}\cRef$ | global displacement of the node |
| Velocity | $\LU{0}{\vv}\cConfig = \Jm_{pos}\dot\qv\cConfig$ | global velocity of the node |
| Acceleration | $\LU{0}{\av}\cConfig = \Jm_{pos}\ddot\qv\cConfig + \dot\Jm_{pos}\dot\qv\cConfig$ | global acceleration of the node |
| RotationMatrix | $\mathrm{vec}(\LU{0n}{\Rot})\cConfig$ | rotation matrix of the node, from rotationMatrixUserFunction, row by row |
| AngularVelocity | $\LU{0}{\tomega}\cConfig = \Jm_{rot}\dot\qv\cConfig$ | global angular velocity of the node |
| AngularVelocityLocal | $\LU{n}{\tomega}\cConfig = \LU{n0}{\Rot}\LU{0}{\tomega}\cConfig$ | local angular velocity of the node |
| CoordinatesTotal |  | displacement plus reference coordinates of node |
| Coordinates | $\qv\cConfig$ | coordinates vector of the node, without the reference values |
| Coordinates_t | $\dot \qv\cConfig$ | velocity coordinates vector of the node |
| Coordinates_tt | $\ddot \qv\cConfig$ | acceleration coordinates vector of the node |

(description-nodeuser)=
## Detailed description

### Coordinates

$n$ = `numberOfODE2Coordinates` {ref}`ODE2 <ODE2>` coordinates; their meaning is defined by the user functions and the
object that uses the node. The user functions get the reference coordinates $\qv\cRef$, the coordinates
$\qv \in \Rcal^n$ **including** their reference values, the velocities $\dot\qv$ and the `parameters` of the node,
as read-only numpy arrays, as the user functions of ObjectUserBody do (#3056).

### Interface of the node

| function | gives | needed for |
|---|---|---|
| `positionUserFunction` | $\LU{0}{\pv}(\qv)$ | positions of markers, sensors and the drawing; must be given |
| `positionJacobianUserFunction` | $\Jm_{pos}(\qv) = \partial \LU{0}{\pv} / \partial \qv$ | forces on MarkerNodePosition, MarkerNodeRigid; by central differences of the position if not given |
| `rotationMatrixUserFunction` | $\LU{0n}{\Rot}(\qv)$ | MarkerNodeRigid, optional |
| `rotationJacobianUserFunction` | $\Jm_{rot}(\qv) = \partial \LU{0}{\tomega} / \partial \dot\qv$ | torques on MarkerNodeRigid; by central differences of the rotation matrix if not given |

The velocity is $\LU{0}{\vv} = \Jm_{pos} \dot\qv$, the acceleration $\LU{0}{\av} = \Jm_{pos} \ddot\qv + \dot\Jm_{pos}
\dot\qv$ with $\dot\Jm_{pos}\dot\qv$ by central differences along $\dot\qv$, the global angular velocity
$\LU{0}{\tomega} = \Jm_{rot} \dot\qv$ and the local one $\LU{n}{\tomega} = \LU{n0}{\Rot}\LU{0}{\tomega}$. Without
a rotation Jacobian, column $k$ of $\Jm_{rot}$ is the axial vector of $(\partial \Rot / \partial q_k) \Rot\tp$, the
derivative by central differences. The derivative of $\Jm_{rot}\tp \mv$ with respect to $\qv$, which the Jacobians
of connectors on MarkerNodeRigid need, is computed by central differences; a MarkerNodePosition treats
$\Jm_{pos}$ as constant in the Jacobians, so a position that is not linear in $\qv$ makes the Newton iteration
converge slower, not wrong.

The user functions are called serially in the main thread; a renderer that runs in a thread of its own draws the
node, the markers on it and what depends on them in the main thread (#3003).

**Userfunction**: `positionUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, qRef, q, q_t, parameters)`
A user function, which computes the global position of the node from its coordinates: the position interface of the node.

| arguments / return | type or size | description |
|---|---|---|
| `mbs` | MainSystem | provides MainSystem mbs to which the node belongs |
| `t` | Real | time of the configuration asked for |
| `itemNumber` | Index | integer number of the node in mbs |
| `qRef` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | the reference coordinates of the node |
| `q` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | node coordinates, INCLUDING their reference values, of the configuration asked for |
| `q_t` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | node velocity coordinates of the configuration asked for; zero in the reference configuration |
| `parameters` | Vector $\in \Rcal^{n_p}$ | the parameters of the node, see parameters; empty if not given |
| **return value** | Vector3D $\in \Rcal^{3}$ | the global position of the node |

A Python user function gets its vector and matrix arguments as read-only numpy arrays, valid during the call, see [](#sec-userfunctions).

**Userfunction**: `positionJacobianUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, qRef, q, q_t, parameters)`
A user function of the interface of the node that returns a matrix: the position Jacobian $\Jm_{pos} = \partial \vv / \partial \dot\qv$ (3 x n), the rotation matrix (3 x 3) or the rotation Jacobian $\Jm_{rot} = \partial \LU{0}{\tomega} / \partial \dot\qv$ (3 x n, global angular velocity).

| arguments / return | type or size | description |
|---|---|---|
| `mbs` | MainSystem | provides MainSystem mbs to which the node belongs |
| `t` | Real | time of the configuration asked for |
| `itemNumber` | Index | integer number of the node in mbs |
| `qRef` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | the reference coordinates of the node |
| `q` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | node coordinates, INCLUDING their reference values, of the configuration asked for |
| `q_t` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | node velocity coordinates of the configuration asked for; zero in the reference configuration |
| `parameters` | Vector $\in \Rcal^{n_p}$ | the parameters of the node, see parameters; empty if not given |
| **return value** | MatrixContainer | the matrix, as numpy array or list of lists |

A Python user function gets its vector and matrix arguments as read-only numpy arrays, valid during the call, see [](#sec-userfunctions).

**Userfunction**: `rotationMatrixUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, qRef, q, q_t, parameters)`
A user function of the interface of the node that returns a matrix: the position Jacobian $\Jm_{pos} = \partial \vv / \partial \dot\qv$ (3 x n), the rotation matrix (3 x 3) or the rotation Jacobian $\Jm_{rot} = \partial \LU{0}{\tomega} / \partial \dot\qv$ (3 x n, global angular velocity).

| arguments / return | type or size | description |
|---|---|---|
| `mbs` | MainSystem | provides MainSystem mbs to which the node belongs |
| `t` | Real | time of the configuration asked for |
| `itemNumber` | Index | integer number of the node in mbs |
| `qRef` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | the reference coordinates of the node |
| `q` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | node coordinates, INCLUDING their reference values, of the configuration asked for |
| `q_t` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | node velocity coordinates of the configuration asked for; zero in the reference configuration |
| `parameters` | Vector $\in \Rcal^{n_p}$ | the parameters of the node, see parameters; empty if not given |
| **return value** | MatrixContainer | the matrix, as numpy array or list of lists |

A Python user function gets its vector and matrix arguments as read-only numpy arrays, valid during the call, see [](#sec-userfunctions).

**Userfunction**: `rotationJacobianUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, qRef, q, q_t, parameters)`
A user function of the interface of the node that returns a matrix: the position Jacobian $\Jm_{pos} = \partial \vv / \partial \dot\qv$ (3 x n), the rotation matrix (3 x 3) or the rotation Jacobian $\Jm_{rot} = \partial \LU{0}{\tomega} / \partial \dot\qv$ (3 x n, global angular velocity).

(miniexample-nodeuser)=
## Mini example


```python
#a node whose coordinates are cylindrical coordinates (r, phi, z) of a point; it turns with phi_t = 1
def UFposition(mbs, t, itemNumber, qRef, q, q_t, parameters):
    return [q[0]*np.cos(q[1]), q[0]*np.sin(q[1]), q[2]]
node = mbs.AddNode(NodeUser(numberOfODE2Coordinates=3, referenceCoordinates=[1,0,0],
                            initialCoordinates=[0,0,0], initialVelocities=[0,1,0],
                            positionUserFunction=UFposition))
#free coordinates with unit mass: phi = t
mbs.AddObject(ObjectGenericODE2(nodeNumbers=[node], massMatrix=np.eye(3)))

mbs.Assemble()
mbs.SolveDynamic()

#after 1 s the position is [cos(1), sin(1), 0]
exu.sys['testResult'] = mbs.GetNodeOutput(node, exu.OutputVariableType.Position)[1] #0.8414709848
```
